effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Anonymous Leaders Reward Protocol specification, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-ledger, logos-blockchain-core or logos-blockchain-poc that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is the LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

Where the specification lives in the code:
- ledger/src/mantle/leader.rs (package `logos-blockchain-ledger`): the ledger's record of unclaimed leader rewards (the voucher or reward commitment per block), the claim window, the reward amount, and the execution of a claim. ledger/src/cryptarchia/mod.rs: where a block's reward entry is created at block application.
- core/src/mantle/ops/leader_claim.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the `LEADER_CLAIM` operation payload. core/src/proofs/leader_claim_proof.rs: the proof of claim's public inputs and verification entry point.
- zk/proofs/poc/src (package `logos-blockchain-poc`): the proof of claim: inputs.rs, chain_inputs.rs, wallet_inputs.rs, witness.rs, lib.rs. The circuit is the prebuilt crate (feature `prebuilt`), outside the repository; what it constrains is 'needs external evidence'.
- Adjacent, outside the unit: the Mantle specification's LEADER_CLAIM section (wire format and validation rules, audited by another brief), wallet/src/voucher.rs (the wallet's side of tracking rewards).

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; core/src/mantle/fixtures/ and ledger/src/mantle/sdp/test_utils.rs show how ledger tests are set up. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
